faqs.a: EMI stands for Equated Monthly Installment — the fixed amount you pay your lender every month until the loan is fully repaid. Each EMI has two parts: interest on the outstanding balance, and principal that reduces what you owe.

With monthly rate r = annual % ÷ 1200 and n = years × 12 payments: EMI = P × r × (1+r)^n ÷ ((1+r)^n − 1). If the interest rate is zero, the EMI is simply the principal divided by the number of months.

Interest is charged on the outstanding balance, which is largest at the start. So the first EMIs are mostly interest with a small principal slice; as the balance shrinks, the interest slice shrinks and the principal slice grows. The yearly table shows this shift.
faqs.q: Why is the interest higher in the early years?

faqs.a: Your monthly EMI goes down, which feels easier — but you pay interest for many more months, so the total interest rises sharply. A 20-year loan can cost nearly double the borrowed amount in total. Shorter terms save interest if you can afford the higher EMI.
faqs.q: What happens if I take a longer loan term?

faqs.a: No. They are typical market rates (Home 8.5%, Personal 11%, Auto 9%) filled in for convenience. Your actual offer depends on your bank, credit score and timing — always replace the preset with the exact rate you were quoted.
faqs.q: Are the preset interest rates exact?

faqs.a: No. The tool computes pure EMI math: principal and interest only. Processing fees, insurance, GST/service charges and prepayment penalties are not included, so treat the result as a planning estimate and confirm the final figures with your lender.
faqs.q: Does this include bank fees and taxes?

loan-calculator.formula: With monthly rate r = annual % ÷ 1200 and n = years × 12 payments: EMI = P·r·(1+r)ⁿ ÷ ((1+r)ⁿ − 1). Total interest = EMI × n − P. When r = 0, EMI = P ÷ n.
howTo: Pick a loan type to fill in a typical rate, or enter your own amount, rate and term.
Set the annual interest rate to the exact figure your bank quoted.
Read your monthly EMI, total interest and total payable at the top.
Scroll the yearly schedule to see how principal and interest split each year.
Try a shorter term or a lower rate to see how much interest you save.
keyFacts: EMI = P × r × (1+r)^n ÷ ((1+r)^n − 1), where r is the monthly rate (annual % ÷ 1200) and n is the number of monthly payments.
Early EMIs are mostly interest; later EMIs are mostly principal — the yearly table shows this shift clearly.
Loan-type presets (Home 8.5%, Personal 11%, Auto 9%) insert typical rates; always edit them to match your actual offer.
A zero interest rate is handled gracefully: EMI simply becomes principal ÷ number of months.
The yearly schedule is capped at 30 rows so it stays readable on phones.
This is a planning estimate; your bank's exact EMI can differ slightly due to rounding, fees and charges.
limitations: Estimates use the standard reducing-balance EMI formula; banks may round differently and add processing fees, insurance and taxes.
Floating-rate loans change over time — this tool assumes your rate stays fixed for the whole term.
It does not model prepayment penalties, late fees or part-payment options.
This is a planning aid, not financial advice — always confirm figures with your lender.

loan-calculator.workedExample: Example: 100,000 at 10% annual for 5 years. Monthly rate r = 10 ÷ 1200 = 0.008333, n = 60 payments. EMI = 100000 × 0.008333 × 1.008333^60 ÷ (1.008333^60 − 1) ≈ 2,124.70 per month. Total payable ≈ 127,482, so total interest ≈ 27,482.
